## Confirmed findings

### 1. `operator>>=` can leave a partially shifted wrong value after `bad_alloc`

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator>>=(size_t)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:548`.

Root: `shift_right_by_bits()` performs the whole-limb shift first at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_right.cpp:62`, then later calls allocation-capable cleanup at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:70` and `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:93`.

Observed effect: a shift by 33 can leave the receiver as `old >> 32`, neither the original value nor the requested `old >> 33`.

Status: confirmed by injected allocation failure probe.

### 2. Copy assignment can leave copied magnitude with stale destination sign after `bad_alloc`

Public route: copy assignment in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:331`.

Root: `copy_to()` commits magnitude/counters, calls `flush_unused()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:89`, and only then copies `_is_negative` at `copy.cpp:90`.

Observed effect: assigning `-7` into a positive destination can leave `+7`.

Status: confirmed by injected allocation failure probe.

### 3. Constructor/allocation path leaks `list_of_int_arrays` if nested allocation throws

Root: `increase_until_num_of_ints()` stores raw `new list_of_int_arrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:270`, then performs nested allocation at `unlimited_int.hpp:271`. If construction throws before the containing `unlimited_int` object is fully constructed, its destructor does not run.

Observed effect: ASan direct leak from constructor/allocation failure.

Status: confirmed with ASan leak probe.

### 4. Reciprocal-cache insertion leaks on allocation failure

Public route: `unlimited_int::recurring_division()`.

Root: `recurring_division()` calls `most_recent.push_front(new size_t(fingerprint_divisor))` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:225`. `custom_linked_list<T>::push_front(T*)` releases the value into `make_unique` before node allocation is guaranteed in `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/custom_linked_list.hpp:101-102`.

Observed effect: ASan direct leak of the allocated `size_t`.

Status: confirmed with ASan leak probe.

### 5. `from_string()` can falsely throw after parsed value is already complete

Public routes: `unlimited_int::from_string(...)`, string constructors, string assignment.

Root: each digit is added at `unlimited/unlimited_int/from_string.cpp:57`, then `multiplicand *= base_ui` runs at `from_string.cpp:59` before checking whether this was the final digit.

Observed effect: parsing `"9"` can throw `bad_alloc` from dead work after the value is already complete.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection reasoning/probe.

### 6. Zero-copy / zero-result paths falsely allocate and can throw

Root: `copy_to()` calls `increase_until_num_of_ints(this_num_of_used_ints)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:20` before checking whether the source is zero at `copy.cpp:22`.

Public paths observed: copy zero, `0+0`, `0|0`, `0^0`, `abs(0)`, `gcd(0,0)`, and `generate_random(0,0)`.

Observed effect: operations whose result is zero can allocate and throw `bad_alloc`.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 7. Public `divide_using_reciprocal()` can corrupt the reciprocal through the `remainder` pointer

Public route: `reciprocal_information::reciprocal` is public in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:50-54`; `divide_using_reciprocal()` is public at `unlimited_int.hpp:386`.

Root: `divide_using_reciprocal()` creates a non-owning view of `*reciprocal.reciprocal` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:68`, then writes to `*remainder` at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:128`.

Observed effect: passing `reciprocal.reciprocal.get()` as `remainder` corrupted the reciprocal. Repro case used dividend `-100`, divisor `7`: first call gave quotient `-14`, reciprocal became `-2`, and the next call threw because the reciprocal was negative.

Status: confirmed by direct public API probe.

### 8. Default build declares `assert_no_memory_leak()` but does not define it

Root: declaration is unconditional at `unlimited/unlimited.hpp:13`; definition is gated behind debug/memory-counting mode in `unlimited/unlimited.cpp:19-24`.

Observed effect: default link probe failed with `undefined reference to unlimited::assert_no_memory_leak()`. The same probe linked when compiled with `-DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=-2`.

Status: confirmed by compile/link probe.

### 9. GNU/Clang 64-bit non-x86_64/non-ppc64 targets are misdetected as 32-bit

Root: GNU platform detection only treats `__x86_64__` and `__ppc64__` as 64-bit in `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/settings.hpp:62-67`.

Observed effect: GNU AArch64/RISC-V 64-bit style targets are classified as 32-bit, conflicting with `fingerprint.cpp` static assertions that expect `sizeof(size_t)` to match `UNLIMITED_INT_COMPILING_ON_64_BIT_SYSTEM`.

Status: source-confirmed portability bug.

### 10. `generate_random_prime()` checks an already-set terminator too late

Root: `generate_random_prime()` calls `generate_random(min, max)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/prime_numbers.cpp:83`, then checks the terminator at `prime_numbers.cpp:84-86`.

Observed effect: with an already-set terminator and `min=max=5`, it returned zero but still performed tracked allocations first.

Status: confirmed by terminator/allocation probe.

### 11. Stream insertion formatting drifts from standard stream flags

Root: stream insertion only selects a base at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:168-176`, then inserts a plain string at `operators.cpp:177`.

Observed effects:

```text
uppercase/showbase hex -> ff
showpos dec -> 7
setbase(0) -> ff
internal width -> '    7'
```

Status: confirmed by stream formatting probe.

### 12. `operator&` can falsely throw after computing the result

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator&(const unlimited_int&)`.

Root: result counters are committed at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_and.cpp:99-101`, then `result.cutoff_leading_zeros(...)` runs at `bitwise_and.cpp:102`.

Observed effect: result is already computed, but cleanup can throw `bad_alloc`.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 13. `operator^` can falsely throw after computing the result

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator^(const unlimited_int&)`.

Root: result counters are committed at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_xor.cpp:141-143`, then `result.cutoff_leading_zeros(...)` runs at `bitwise_xor.cpp:144`.

Observed effect: result is already computed, but cleanup can throw `bad_alloc`.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 14. Sign-changing `operator+=` / `operator-=` can leave stale sign after late cleanup failure

Public routes: `operator+=` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:400`; `operator-=` at `unlimited_int.hpp:403`.

Root: subtraction main path commits magnitude/counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, calls `cutoff_leading_zeros()` at `subtraction.cpp:377`, then fixes sign at `subtraction.cpp:378-381`.

Observed effect: `(2^9000 - 1) -= 2^9000` can be left as `+1` instead of `-1`; symmetric `+=` sign-changing case exists.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 15. `--x` / retained-storage zero can leave `+1` instead of `-1`

Public route: `operator--()` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:102`.

Root: retained-storage zero routes through the zero-minus branch in `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:20-37`; `copy_to()` can throw before the sign flip.

Observed setup: create a large value, subtract it from itself to get zero while retaining storage, then decrement under injected allocation failure.

Observed effect: receiver can become `+1` where `-1` is expected.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 16. `invert_bits()` on retained-storage zero has the same stale-sign failure shape

Public route: `unlimited_int::invert_bits()`.

Root: `invert_bits()` does `++(*this)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_not.cpp:45`, then flips/clears sign at `bitwise_not.cpp:46-49`. The increment can throw after producing `+1` but before sign inversion.

Observed effect: retained-storage zero can become `+1` instead of `-1`.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 17. `generate_random_prime(min, max)` validates `max < min` too late

Root: computes `unlimited_int range_size(max - min)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/prime_numbers.cpp:77`, then checks negativity at `prime_numbers.cpp:78-79`.

Observed effect: for `min > max`, injected allocation failure can produce `bad_alloc` before the expected `invalid_argument`.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe.

### 18. `from_string()` can allocate before validating an invalid digit

Public route: `unlimited_int::from_string(const char*, unsigned)` and `unlimited_int::from_string(const std::string&, unsigned)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:581-583`.

Root: `from_string_range()` validates base/null/empty/minus and skips leading zeroes, then constructs `unlimited_int base_ui((few_bits)base)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/from_string.cpp:44` before checking any digit in the loop at `from_string.cpp:50`. For any nonzero invalid digit that survives the leading-zero skip, allocation can happen before the invalid digit is reported.

Observed effect: `from_string("2" + many zeroes, 2)` normally throws `invalid_argument`, but injected failure at the first allocation produces `bad_alloc` before the invalid digit is checked.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_from_string_invalid_probe`: `from_string_invalid_probe=bad_alloc_before_invalid fail_at=1 allocations_seen=1`.

### 19. Out-of-place subtraction can falsely throw after the result has been computed

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator-(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:404`, implemented through `unlimited_int::subtract(...)`.

Root: subtraction writes the result magnitude, commits `answer->num_of_used_ints`, `answer->num_of_intarrays_used`, and the current int_array's `num_of_used_ints` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls allocation-capable cleanup at `subtraction.cpp:377` before applying the final sign at `subtraction.cpp:378-381`.

Observed effect: `(2^9000 - 1) - 2^9000` should return `-1`, but allocation failure in the cleanup-only window makes the out-of-place operator throw `bad_alloc` after the full-width arithmetic work is already done. This is distinct from finding 14: finding 14 is the in-place stale-sign state left in the receiver, while this route loses the already-computed out-of-place result by throwing.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_subtract_false_throw_probe`: `subtract_false_throw=confirmed full_width_allocations=10 shrink_allocations=12 cleanup_fail_at=11`.

### 20. `calculate_reciprocal_floor()` can return a non-floor reciprocal for short supported dividend lengths

Public route: `unlimited_int::calculate_reciprocal_floor(size_t)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:382`.

Root: when `length_dividend_to_support < this->num_of_used_ints`, `calculate_reciprocal_floor()` immediately returns reciprocal `1` and `amount_shifted = this->num_of_used_ints` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:13-14`, skipping the Newton-Raphson path whose comment defines the target as `floor(B^k / N)`.

Observed effect: for divisor `0x100000001` (`2^32 + 1`) and `length_dividend_to_support = 1`, the function returns `amount_shifted=2` and `reciprocal=1`. The exact floored reciprocal for the returned shift amount is `floor(2^64 / (2^32 + 1)) = 0xffffffff`, so the public helper's returned reciprocal is not the floored reciprocal described by the function name/header comment. Division with that reciprocal is still sufficient for supported one-limb dividends because every such dividend is smaller than the two-limb divisor and the quotient is always zero; the bug is the direct public reciprocal value/contract, not a wrong quotient on the supported divide path.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_recip_short_probe.cpp`: `amount=2`, `reciprocal=1`, while Python exact arithmetic gives `0xffffffff`.

### 21. Out-of-place `operator<<` can throw `bad_alloc` before validating a negative operand

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator<<(size_t)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:574-578`.

Root: the out-of-place wrapper first copy-constructs `answer` from `*this` at `unlimited_int.hpp:575`, then calls `answer <<= num_to_shift_by` at `unlimited_int.hpp:576`. The actual negative-operand validation lives inside `shift_left_by_bits()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_left.cpp:84-86`, after the copy has already allocated through `copy_to()` / `increase_until_num_of_ints()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:20`). The in-place `operator<<=` path reaches the validation before allocation, but the out-of-place wrapper does not.

Observed effect: for a negative operand, injected allocation failure during the copy makes `x << 1` throw `std::bad_alloc` before the documented `std::invalid_argument`. The matching in-place `x <<= 1` throws `invalid_argument` under the same setup.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_negative_shift_validation_probe.cpp`: `inplace_left=invalid_argument`, `out_left=bad_alloc_before_invalid`.

Root: the out-of-place wrapper first copy-constructs `answer` from `*this` at `unlimited_int.hpp:569`, then calls `answer >>= num_to_shift_by` at `unlimited_int.hpp:570`. The actual negative-operand validation lives inside `shift_right_by_bits()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_right.cpp:58-59`, after the copy has already allocated through `copy_to()` / `increase_until_num_of_ints()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:20`). The in-place `operator>>=` path reaches the validation before allocation, but the out-of-place wrapper does not.

### 23. Accepted `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=0` configuration makes public construction hang

Public route: compile with the supported command-line override `-DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=0`, then construct any nonzero public `unlimited_int`, for example `unlimited::unlimited_int x(1)`.

Root: the settings header accepts the override at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/settings.hpp:45-49`, and the only visible allocation-parameter validation is `static_assert(MAX_ALLOC >= MIN_ALLOC || MIN_ALLOC <= 0, ...)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/int_array.cpp:230`. Because `MIN_ALLOC` is a `size_t`, `MIN_ALLOC=0` is accepted. A first allocation enters `unlimited_int::increase_until_num_of_ints()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:267-271`, then `list_of_int_arrays::increase_until_num_of_ints()` loops while `num_of_ints` is too small at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/list_of_int_arrays.cpp:41-45`. With `num_of_ints == 0` and `MIN_ALLOC == 0`, `increase_by_one_array()` computes `current_len_arr_to_add == 0` at `list_of_int_arrays.cpp:25-29`, appends a zero-length node at `list_of_int_arrays.cpp:32-35`, and increments total capacity by zero at `list_of_int_arrays.cpp:37`. The loop therefore makes no progress.

Observed effect: `/tmp/unlimited_int_min_alloc_zero_probe` compiled successfully with `-DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=0 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=256`, but `timeout 3s /tmp/unlimited_int_min_alloc_zero_probe` exited with status `124` while doing only `unlimited::unlimited_int x(1);`.

Status: confirmed by accepted-configuration timeout probe.

### 24. `operator*=` can leave a negative receiver positive after `bad_alloc`

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator*=(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:362`.

Root: `operator*=` saves the original signs at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:37-38`, then immediately clears the receiver's sign at `operators.cpp:39` before entering allocation-capable multiplication paths. In the small-value path, line `operators.cpp:55` assigns the native product back through the public native assignment wrapper (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:323-324` on this platform), which constructs a temporary `unlimited_int`. That temporary construction allocates through `assign(many_bits)` / `increase_until_num_of_ints()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/assign.cpp:149-190`) before the original sign is restored at `operators.cpp:61-63`.

Observed effect: with `x == -7` and `y == 3`, forcing the first allocation inside `x *= y` to throw leaves `x == +7` instead of preserving the original `-7`. This is a public mutating operation producing a wrong surviving receiver value after `std::bad_alloc`.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_mul_sign_probe.cpp`: output `bad_alloc_value 7`. Follow-up sweep `/tmp/unlimited_int_mulassign_sweep_probe.cpp` reproduced the same root for small, power-of-two, and large negative receivers: fail index 0 leaves the magnitude unchanged but flips the surviving sign positive.

### 25. Copy assignment can throw `bad_alloc` after fully committing the new value

Public route: copy assignment in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:331`.

Root: `copy_to()` copies the source magnitude into the destination, commits `num_of_intarrays_used` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:87`, commits the last array's used count at `copy.cpp:88`, and only then calls `flush_unused()` at `copy.cpp:89`. `flush_unused()` may call `flush_significant_to_piggy_bank()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:166-170`), which can allocate a temporary sublist object through `int_array_piggy_bank::deposit_from_significant()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/int_array_piggy_bank.cpp:21` and `int_array_list::sublist_int_array_list()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/int_array_list.cpp:26-27`. If that cleanup allocation throws, the destination has already been changed to the source value even though the public assignment reports failure.

Observed effect: assigning a small positive source into a larger positive target and forcing the first cleanup allocation to fail leaves the target equal to the source (`7`) while throwing `std::bad_alloc`.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_copy_assign_false_throw_probe.cpp`: `copy_assign_false_throw fail=0 before=123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0 after=7`.

### 26. `generate_random_prime()` hangs forever for a singleton composite range

Public route: `unlimited_int::generate_random_prime(min, max)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/prime_numbers.cpp:74-89`.

Root: the function validates only `max < min` by computing `range_size(max - min)` at `prime_numbers.cpp:77-79`, then repeatedly samples `current_try = unlimited_int::generate_random(min, max)` at `prime_numbers.cpp:83` until `current_try.is_prime(64, terminator)` succeeds at `prime_numbers.cpp:87`. For a singleton composite range, `generate_random(min, max)` deterministically returns `min` through its equality shortcut at `unlimited/unlimited_int/generate_random.cpp:214-217`. With the default null terminator, the loop has no exit and no random chance of success.

Observed effect: `unlimited_int::generate_random_prime(unlimited_int(4), unlimited_int(4))` never returns and never throws. This is not probabilistic: the only candidate is always `4`, and `4.is_prime()` is always false.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_prime_free_hang_probe.cpp`; `timeout 3s /tmp/unlimited_int_prime_free_hang_probe` exited with status `124`.

### 27. Raw-array `assign()` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing a leading-zero value

Protected/documented route: `unlimited_int::assign(const uint32_t*, size_t)` and `unlimited_int::assign(const uint64_t*, size_t)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/assign.cpp:6-57` and `assign.cpp:58-121`. The header comments on these protected helpers say they are used by the raw-array constructors but "can also be used independently" (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:103-111`), so a derived user can expose the route directly.

Root: raw-array assignment writes the incoming limbs, commits `num_of_used_ints` and `num_of_intarrays_used` at `assign.cpp:46-49` for `uint32_t` input and `assign.cpp:110-113` for `uint64_t` input, then calls `cutoff_leading_zeros()`. That helper adjusts the committed used counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-37` and then calls `flush_unused()`. If the leading zero limbs remove only some significant nodes, `flush_unused()` reaches `int_array_piggy_bank::deposit_from_significant()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/int_array_piggy_bank.cpp:21`, which allocates temporary sublist objects through `int_array_list::sublist_int_array_list()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/int_array_list.cpp:26-27`.

Observed effect: assigning a `uint32_t` big-endian raw array with a leading zero limb can throw `std::bad_alloc` from the cleanup path while the object is already equal to the intended stripped value. In the probe, the object reports failure but survives as `0x123456789abcdef013579bdf2468ace0`.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_raw_assign_badalloc_probe.cpp` under `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1` and `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2`: output `false bad_alloc after commit at allocation 4`.

### 28. Large public `operator*=` can leave the receiver as zero after `bad_alloc`

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator*=(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:362`, implemented at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:35-82`.

Root: for non-small, non-power-of-two operands, `operator*=` calls the destructive Karatsuba helper at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:74-75`: `*this = this->multiply_karatsuba_destroy_this(&other)`. The helper then calls `this->split_at_and_use_original(m2, &high1, &low1)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/multiplication_Karatsuba.cpp:161-164`. In `split_at_and_use_original()`, the least-significant part is detached from the receiver at `unlimited/unlimited_int/split_at.cpp:261-263`, then the receiver's counters are reset to zero at `split_at.cpp:264-266`, while later allocation-capable work still remains (`high->increase_until_num_of_ints(...)` at `split_at.cpp:271-272` and the high-side `sublist_int_array_list(...)` transfer at `split_at.cpp:342-343`). If one of those later allocations throws, the public receiver survives with the already-committed destructive split state.

Observed effect: a large positive `x *= y` where both operands are above the Karatsuba threshold can throw `std::bad_alloc` and leave `x == 0`, even though `x` was a nonzero positive integer before the call. This is distinct from finding 24: finding 24 is the early sign-clear path leaving a negative receiver positive; this finding is the destructive Karatsuba split path changing the surviving magnitude of a positive receiver.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_karatsuba_badalloc_probe.cpp`. The default allocation geometry reproduced it:

```text
karatsuba_badalloc_mutation case=positive_karatsuba_times_equal allocation=12 before=feeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee after=0
```

The same probe also reproduced under ASan/UBSan with `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1`, `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1`, and `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2`.

### 29. Public `operator%=` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing the correct remainder

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator%=(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:150-156`.

Root: `operator%=` first computes `answer_divide` and `answer_multiply`, then mutates the receiver in place through `this->subtract(&answer_multiply, this)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:155`. The subtraction helper commits the result counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls `answer->cutoff_leading_zeros(it_answer)` at `subtraction.cpp:377`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` updates the used counters for the shortened value at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36`, then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`. If that cleanup allocation throws, the public `%=` call reports `std::bad_alloc` even though the receiver has already been changed to the final remainder.

Observed effect: `x %= y` can throw `std::bad_alloc` while leaving `x` equal to the mathematically correct remainder instead of preserving the pre-call value. This is distinct from finding 14's stale-sign in-place subtraction failure and finding 19's out-of-place subtraction false throw: this is the public remainder-assignment wrapper committing its result before reporting failure.

Status: confirmed first by `/tmp/unlimited_int_public_mutation_fault_scan2.cpp` under ASan/UBSan, debug mode, `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1`, and `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2`: `mod_large_by_large allocation=86` changed the receiver to the exact Python-verified remainder. Dedicated repro `/tmp/unlimited_int_modassign_false_throw_probe2.cpp` confirmed `modassign_false_throw_after_commit allocation=86`.

The same class also reproduced under default allocation geometry with `/tmp/unlimited_int_modassign_default_search.cpp`:

```text
modassign_changed_default dividend_len=1400 divisor_len=700 allocation=900 after_len=700
after_prefix=49151f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a
after_tail=1f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a598ec9151f42bef1a3100d84a598e
```

Independent Python arithmetic for `int("f" + "e"*1399, 16) % int("d" + "7"*699, 16)` produced the same 700-hex-digit prefix and tail.

### 30. Public `operator++` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing the increment result

Public route: pre-increment `unlimited_int::operator++()` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:96-100`; post-increment delegates to it at `operators.cpp:108-110`.

Root: `operator++()` constructs `one` and calls public `operator+=` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:400`). If the receiver is numerically zero but still owns extra int-array nodes, `unlimited_int::add()` takes the zero-left branch at `unlimited/unlimited_int/addition.cpp:16-22` and copies `one` into the receiver through `copy_to()`. `copy_to()` commits the destination counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:87-88` and only then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `copy.cpp:89`; `flush_unused()` can call `flush_significant_to_piggy_bank()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:166-170`), which reaches the partial-sublist allocation in `int_array_piggy_bank.cpp:21` / `int_array_list.cpp:26-27`.

Observed effect: create a large value, subtract it from itself to get zero while retaining storage, then force allocation failure during `++x`. The public operation throws `std::bad_alloc` while leaving `x == 1`, i.e. the increment result was committed even though the call reported failure.

This is distinct from finding #25's copy-assignment surface because the public operation is increment, and distinct from #15/#16 because the expected result of `++x` is `+1`; the bug here is a false failure after successful mutation, not stale sign.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_increment_retained_zero_probe.cpp` under ASan/UBSan, debug mode, `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1`, and `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2`:

```text
increment_retained_zero_changed_after_bad_alloc allocation=4 before=0 after=1
```

### 31. Public `recurring_division()` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing output `remainder`

Public route: `unlimited_int::recurring_division(const unlimited_int& dividend, const unlimited_int& divisor, unlimited_int* remainder)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:150-173`.

Root: in the `|dividend| < |divisor|` branch, `recurring_division()` writes the caller-provided output parameter with `*remainder = dividend` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:171-172`, then returns a zero quotient. That assignment goes through public copy assignment at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:331`, which calls `copy_to()`. `copy_to()` commits the destination's used-array and used-limb counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:87-88` before calling allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `copy.cpp:89`. If the caller's `remainder` already owns extra retained storage, `flush_unused()` can fail while depositing the unused tail, after the visible output value has already been changed to the final remainder.

Observed effect: `recurring_division(7, 1000, &remainder)` can throw `std::bad_alloc` while leaving `remainder == 7`. The quotient calculation reports failure, but the caller-visible output parameter has already been committed.

This shares the same late-cleanup root as finding #25, but it is a distinct public API surface: the caller did not explicitly assign to `remainder`; the division wrapper mutates its output parameter and then reports failure. It is also distinct from finding #7, which is reciprocal-output alias corruption, not a false failure after committing the mathematically correct remainder.

Status: confirmed by `/tmp/unlimited_int_recurring_remainder_false_commit_probe.cpp` under ASan/UBSan, debug mode, `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1`, and `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2`:

```text
recurring_remainder_false_commit allocation=0 before=123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0 after=7
```

## Demoted or rejected candidates

- `power2_destroy_this()` source consumption on allocation failure: destructive helper semantics; not promoted without public wrong-value/corruption proof.
- `operator<<=` cleanup/exception suspicion: recent `shift_left` design reserves before mutation; no partial wrong shift confirmed.
- Self-move: excluded by project memory/high bar.
- Other arbitrary/internal configuration constants set to zero: excluded by project memory/high bar unless the configuration is accepted through the public build interface and produces an ordinary public API failure, as in finding 23.
- Theoretical `size_t` overflow: excluded without reachable reproduction.
- RNG security commentary: excluded; not arithmetic/reachability bug.
- Null pointer to protected/internal helper params: excluded unless public route exists.
- Negative `is_prime`: not a bug; header documents sign ignored, e.g. `-2` prime.
- `custom_linked_list<T>::push_back(T*)` / `insert(T*)` leak shape: same raw-pointer release issue as `push_front`, but no confirmed public route yet.
- `operator|` late `cutoff_leading_zeros`: rechecked after the `operator&`/`operator^` false-throw findings; not promoted because the top limb comes from the longer nonzero operand, valid inputs do not reduce `num_of_intarrays_used`, and `flush_unused()` has no unused node to deposit in that case.
- `number_to_char()` validates `num >= base` before validating `base`: not promoted; no allocation/state mutation/arithmetic effect, and the visible exception category remains `out_of_range`.
- `%=` exact-division-to-zero stale sign suspicion: rejected after source read; exact-equal subtraction path uses `set_to_zero()` early.
- `generate_random.cpp` forward declaration `many_bits ceiling_division(many_bits, many_bits)` vs later `size_t ceiling_division(size_t, size_t)`: rejected after source-order review; the `size_t` definition appears before the public calls, so overload resolution picks the local `size_t` overload for the current callers. A 32-bit compile probe could not run in this environment because multilib C++ headers are missing.
- `copy_most_significant_to()` mutates the destination sign before allocation, but current public routes use scratch/output objects where late failure has not been shown to leave a public object with a wrong arithmetic value. Not promoted.
- `shift_left` / `operator<<=` exception suspicion re-read against current source: the current implementation reserves additional list capacity before the in-place limb/bit shift and the late spare-node cleanup is pointer-only/deposit-only for the inspected path. No new public wrong-value finding.
- `sha256.cpp` / `sha512.cpp` signed-index warnings from a strong-warning compile were re-read; the warned `int index_in_block` values are bounded to `0..15` before conversion to `size_t`. Existing hash differential coverage still stands; not promoted.
- GCC `-fanalyzer` warning pass was noisy and did not produce a new promoted issue. The visible warnings were either known candidates already tracked here, standard-library allocation false positives, delete-after-deref notes for non-null internal list nodes, or analyzer confusion around `unlimited_int` / list-node default initialization that is covered by constructors and debug-mode probes.
- `copy_most_significant_to()` zero-length-copy suspicion: the helper would not handle `num_of_ints_to_copy == 0`, but the only current callers are division paths that pass a positive divisor/window length after zero-divisor and magnitude guards. No public route promoted.
- `list_of_int_arrays::{increase_by_one_array,increase_by_one_array_and_zero,increase_by_one_array_to_insignificant}` raw node/value allocation shape: re-read after recent hardening. The temporary node owns and deletes the raw `int_array` value if backing allocation throws, and `int_array::resize()` leaves no half-owned array on failed `new`. No public leak/state bug promoted from this pattern.
- `generate_truly_random()` hash-zero dereference suspicion remains non-reproducible/probabilistic only: it dereferences `num_to_return.intarrays` after hashing the seed, but a zero cryptographic hash would be required for the public route. Not promoted without deterministic input reachability.
- Non-modular sliding-window `pow()` with negative bases rechecked: the sign is reset by later squarings unless the final nonzero exponent window reaches the least-significant bit, which matches the expected negative-only-when-exponent-is-odd behavior. Existing signed window probe still stands; not promoted.

### 32. Same-sign public `operator-=` / `operator--` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing the subtraction result

Public routes: `unlimited_int::operator-=(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:403`, plus pre-decrement `unlimited_int::operator--()` and post-decrement `unlimited_int::operator--(int)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:102-115`.

Root: `operator--()` constructs `one` and delegates to `(*this) -= one` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:104-105`. The main subtraction path writes the result, commits `answer->num_of_used_ints`, `answer->num_of_intarrays_used`, and the current int-array's used count at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls `answer->cutoff_leading_zeros(it_answer)` at `subtraction.cpp:377`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` updates the receiver's counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36` and then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`.

Observed effect: subtracting from a positive value in a way that shrinks leading zero limbs can leave the receiver equal to the exact expected result while still throwing `std::bad_alloc` from the cleanup-only window. The concrete reproducer uses public decrement on `2^4096`, leaving the receiver equal to `2^4096 - 1`.

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_decrement_false_commit_probe.cpp`.

Build:

```bash
g++ --std=c++20 -m64 -I/home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/*.cpp /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/unlimited_int/*.cpp /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/*.cpp /tmp/unlimited_int_decrement_false_commit_probe.cpp -o /tmp/unlimited_int_decrement_false_commit_probe -Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2
```

Run output:

```text
decrement_false_throw_after_commit allocation=4 expected_prefix=ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff expected_tail=ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #15's retained-zero stale-sign bug (`--0` can become `+1` instead of `-1`), and not finding #14's sign-changing `operator-=` stale-sign bug. Here the public same-sign subtraction/decrement leaves the receiver as the correct positive result and still reports failure. It is the decrement/subtraction-side counterpart to finding #30's public increment false commit, with a different subtraction/cutoff root.

Status: confirmed by allocation-injection probe. Promoted count is now 32.

### 33. Opposite-sign public `operator+=` / negative `operator++` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing the addition result

Public routes: `unlimited_int::operator+=(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:400`, plus pre-increment `unlimited_int::operator++()` and post-increment `unlimited_int::operator++(int)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:96-110`.

When the operands have opposite signs, `add()` strips signs and delegates to `subtract()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/addition.cpp:66-73`. The subtraction path writes the result magnitude, commits `answer->num_of_used_ints`, `answer->num_of_intarrays_used`, and the current int-array's used count at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls `answer->cutoff_leading_zeros(it_answer)` at `subtraction.cpp:377`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` updates the receiver's counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36` and then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`.

### 34. Opposite-sign public `operator+` can throw `bad_alloc` after computing the result

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator+(const unlimited_int&)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:84-88`.

Root: `operator+` creates a local `answer` and calls `this->add(&other, &answer)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:85-86`. For opposite-sign operands, `add()` strips signs and delegates to `subtract()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/addition.cpp:66-76`. The subtraction path writes the result magnitude, commits `answer->num_of_used_ints`, `answer->num_of_intarrays_used`, and the current int-array's used count at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls `answer->cutoff_leading_zeros(it_answer)` at `subtraction.cpp:377`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` updates the result counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36` and then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`.

Observed effect: `(2^9000 - 1) + (-2^9000)` should return `-1`, but an allocation failure in the cleanup-only window makes public `operator+` throw `std::bad_alloc` after the full-width arithmetic work has already produced the result in its local output object. The caller loses the already-computed `-1`; both input operands remain unchanged.

### 36. Public `divide_using_reciprocal()` accepts a zero reciprocal despite the positive-reciprocal precondition

Public route: `unlimited_int::divide_using_reciprocal(const unlimited_int&, const reciprocal_information&, const unlimited_int&, unlimited_int*)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:386`.

Root: the public header says the supplied reciprocal "must be with enough precision and also be positive" and that otherwise an exception is thrown at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:383`. The implementation validates a null reciprocal at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:61-62` and a negative reciprocal at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:63-64`, but it never rejects zero. With `reciprocal.reciprocal == 0`, `reciprocal_shifted` is zero, the initial quotient estimate becomes zero at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:77-79`, and the correction path at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:96-101` increments the answer and multiplication result one divisor at a time until it passes the dividend.

Observed effect: a caller-supplied zero reciprocal is accepted by the public API even though it is not positive. For `dividend = 1000`, `divisor = 1`, and `amount_shifted = 4`, the call returns quotient `1000` and remainder `0` instead of throwing. For larger quotients, the same path becomes a quotient-sized correction loop, which defeats the Newton-Raphson API's expected precision contract and can turn a division call into unbounded repeated addition work.

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_zero_reciprocal_probe.cpp`.

Build:

```bash
g++ --std=c++20 -m64 -I/home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/*.cpp /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/unlimited_int/*.cpp /home/user/Desktop/unlimited_int/unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/*.cpp /tmp/unlimited_int_zero_reciprocal_probe.cpp -o /tmp/unlimited_int_zero_reciprocal_probe -Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2
```

Run output:

```text
zero_reciprocal_accepted quotient=1000 remainder=0
negative_reciprocal_rejected
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #7's reciprocal-output alias corruption and not finding #20's short-support `calculate_reciprocal_floor()` contract bug. The caller directly supplies a public `reciprocal_information` whose reciprocal is zero; `divide_using_reciprocal()` advertises rejection of non-positive reciprocals but accepts this one and falls into its correction loop.

Status: confirmed by direct public API repro. Promoted count is now 36.

### 37. Public `operator>>=` can throw `bad_alloc` after committing the complete shifted result

Public route: `unlimited_int::operator>>=(size_t)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:548`.

Root: `operator>>=` delegates to `shift_right_by_bits()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_right.cpp:49-102`). For a non-whole-limb shift, `shift_right_by_bits()` first performs the whole-limb shift at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:62`, then performs the in-place micro-shift loop at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:73-92`, and finally calls `cutoff_leading_zeros()` at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:93`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` commits the shortened used-node/used-limb counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36`, then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`. `flush_unused()` can allocate through partial piggy-bank deposit at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:166-170`.

Observed effect: with an ordinary reused public object, `x >>= 33` can throw `std::bad_alloc` after `x` is already equal to the exact result `old_x >> 33`. The dedicated reproducer first creates an oversized public receiver, assigns the target value normally with faults disabled, then injects allocation failure during the right shift. The receiver survives as the complete shifted value even though the public operation reports failure.

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_shift_right_false_commit_probe.cpp`.

Build:

```bash
g++ --std=c++20 -m64 unlimited/*.cpp unlimited/unlimited_int/*.cpp unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/*.cpp /tmp/unlimited_int_shift_right_false_commit_probe.cpp -I. -o /tmp/unlimited_int_shift_right_false_commit_probe -Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -O1 -g -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2
```

Run output:

```text
shift_right_false_throw_after_commit allocation=2 expected_tail=0000000000000000000000000091a2b3
```

Distinctness: this is not the same observed effect as finding #1. Finding #1 is the same public operator leaving a wrong partially shifted receiver (`old >> 32` for a requested `old >> 33`) after `bad_alloc`. This finding is the later cleanup window where the full micro-shift and counter updates have completed, the receiver equals the mathematically correct `old >> 33`, and the call still throws from cleanup. A fix that makes right shift all-or-nothing would likely address both, but the surviving public state is different.

Status: confirmed by a dedicated public API allocation-injection repro and by the broader `/tmp/unlimited_int_fault_mutating_classifier.cpp` sweep, which classified this state twice under `shift_right_assign_known_1`: `bad_allocs=4 [unchanged:2] [candidate #37 committed right shift:2]`. Promoted count is now 37.

### 38. `invert_bits()` can leave a negative receiver at `x + 1` after `bad_alloc`

Public route: `unlimited_int::invert_bits()` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_not.cpp:35-57`.

Root: `invert_bits()` implements `~x` as `-(x + 1)` by first calling `++(*this)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_not.cpp:45`, then flipping or clearing the sign at `bitwise_not.cpp:46-49`. For a negative nonzero receiver, `operator++()` delegates to `operator+=` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/operators.cpp:96-100`. The opposite-sign addition path delegates into subtraction at `unlimited/unlimited_int/addition.cpp:68-73`; subtraction commits the new magnitude and counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/subtraction.cpp:374-376`, then calls `cutoff_leading_zeros()` at `subtraction.cpp:377`. `cutoff_leading_zeros()` commits shortened counters at `unlimited/unlimited_int/strip_significant_zeros.cpp:35-36` and then calls allocation-capable `flush_unused()` at `strip_significant_zeros.cpp:37`. If that cleanup throws, control never returns to `invert_bits()`, so the sign flip needed for the bitwise-not result never happens.

Observed effect: for `x = -1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035349`, the correct in-place `invert_bits()` result is `1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035348`. With injected allocation failure, the call throws `std::bad_alloc` while leaving `x == -1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035348`, i.e. the intermediate `x + 1` value with the wrong sign for the requested public operation.

Minimal release-mode probe transcript using `/tmp/unlimited_int_fault_probe_release`:

```text
command: mut invert 5 -1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035349 0 0
output: bad_alloc other:-1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035348 allocs=1642
original: -1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035349
expected: 1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035348
observed: -1569275433846670190958947355881144766539853198709676035348
```

Distinctness: this is adjacent to finding #16 and the public `operator++` false-commit findings, but it is a distinct public `invert_bits()` wrong-state class. Finding #16 covers retained-storage zero becoming `+1` instead of `-1`; this case does not require retained-storage zero and leaves a negative nonzero receiver at the intermediate increment result instead of the positive bitwise-not result. Finding #33 covers negative `operator++` reporting failure after committing the increment result; this finding is the higher-level `invert_bits()` operation failing before its required sign inversion.

Status: confirmed by release-mode allocation-failure injection with the public API only. Promoted count is now 38.

### 39. Protected non-owning constructor can free another live integer when `auto_destroy_this=true`

Protected/documented route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`. The header comment says it receives another `unlimited_int` "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy` in the new object. A derived class can expose this protected constructor directly, the same subclass-accessible category as the protected raw-array `assign()` route in finding #27.

Root: the constructor aliases the source object's backing storage pointer at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`:

```cpp
this->auto_destroy = auto_destroy_this;
this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays;
```

If `auto_destroy_this` is `true`, the alias destructor respects that flag at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:654-659` and calls `flush()`. `flush()` deletes `this->intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.cpp:14-23`. Because the aliased source object still contains the same `intarrays` pointer, the source becomes a live object with a dangling backing list.

Observed effect: a derived test class exposed the protected constructor, constructed `exposed_unlimited_int owning_alias(original, true)`, destroyed the alias, and then called `original.to_string(10)`. AddressSanitizer reported a heap-use-after-free while copying/inspecting the original:

```text
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free
READ of size 8
#0 unlimited::unlimited_int::find_inconsistencies() const unlimited/unlimited_int/find_inconsistencies.cpp:29
#1 unlimited::unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited::unlimited_int&) const unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:13
#2 unlimited::unlimited_int::unlimited_int(unlimited::unlimited_int const&) unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:311
#3 unlimited::unlimited_int::to_string(unsigned int) const unlimited/unlimited_int/to_string.cpp:23
#4 main /tmp/unlimited_int_view_ctor_probe.cpp:20
freed by:
#1 unlimited::unlimited_int::flush() unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.cpp:20
#2 unlimited::unlimited_int::~unlimited_int() unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:659
```

The same probe rewritten to pass `false` for the second argument printed the original value successfully under ASan/UBSan, so the failure is specifically the documented ownership flag rather than a generic derived-test harness issue.

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_view_ctor_probe.cpp`, built with:

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O0 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_view_ctor_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_view_ctor_probe
```

Status: confirmed by ASan/UBSan with a derived-class exposure of the documented protected constructor. Promoted count is now 39.

### 40. Public `divide_using_reciprocal()` accepts a positive but unrelated reciprocal and can enter a quotient-sized correction loop

Public route: `unlimited_int::divide_using_reciprocal(const unlimited_int&, const reciprocal_information&, const unlimited_int&, unlimited_int*)` in `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:386`, with caller-constructible `reciprocal_information` fields exposed publicly at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:50-55`.

Root: the public header says the reciprocal "must be with enough precision and also be positive" and that otherwise an exception is thrown at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:383`. The implementation only checks for a null reciprocal, a negative reciprocal, and a large-enough `amount_shifted` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/Newton_Raphson.cpp:61-66`. It does not validate that the positive reciprocal value is actually a reciprocal for the supplied divisor. A forged positive value like `reciprocal.reciprocal = 1` and a sufficiently large `amount_shifted` passes the checks, produces an initial quotient that is far too small at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:77-79`, then falls into the correction loop at `Newton_Raphson.cpp:96-101`. That loop increments `answer` and `result_multiplication` one divisor at a time until the product passes the dividend.

Observed effect: a small forged positive reciprocal is accepted instead of rejected:

```text
small_positive_bad_reciprocal_accepted quotient=333 remainder=1
```

For a larger dividend, the same public route does not finish within the timeout because the correction loop has degraded into repeated addition proportional to the quotient:

```text
small_positive_bad_reciprocal_accepted quotient=333 remainder=1
starting_large_positive_bad_reciprocal
```

The command `timeout 3s /tmp/unlimited_int_bad_positive_reciprocal_probe` exited with status `124`.

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_bad_positive_reciprocal_probe.cpp`.

Build and run:

```bash
g++ --std=c++20 -m64 unlimited/*.cpp unlimited/unlimited_int/*.cpp unlimited/unlimited_int/structures/*.cpp /tmp/unlimited_int_bad_positive_reciprocal_probe.cpp -I. -o /tmp/unlimited_int_bad_positive_reciprocal_probe -Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=0
timeout 3s /tmp/unlimited_int_bad_positive_reciprocal_probe
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #36. Finding #36 is the non-positive reciprocal gap: `reciprocal == 0` violates the advertised positive precondition and should be rejected. This finding uses a strictly positive reciprocal (`1`) with a large-enough shift, so a fix that only rejects zero reciprocals would still leave this public route. It is also not finding #20, because the bad reciprocal is caller-supplied through the public struct rather than returned by `calculate_reciprocal_floor()`, and not finding #7, because no output/remainder aliasing is involved.

Status: confirmed by direct public API repro with a small accepted case plus a deterministic timeout case. Promoted count is now 40.

### 41. Release-mode public assignment through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view writes through and corrupts the source

Protected/documented route plus public assignment route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`, where the header says it receives another integer "without copying" and that the second argument decides `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose that constructor with `auto_destroy_this=false`, then use the inherited public copy assignment operator at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:331`.

Root: the constructor implementation aliases the source storage directly by copying `num_to_assign.intarrays` into the view at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`. Copy assignment calls `copy_to(*this)` through the public wrapper at `unlimited_int.hpp:331`. `copy_to()` has the exact needed non-owning-destination guard, but that guard is inside `#if UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE > 0` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:12-17`, so normal release/default builds compile it out. After that, `copy_to()` unconditionally sets the destination to owning at `copy.cpp:18`, ensures capacity at `copy.cpp:20`, and writes the source limbs through the destination's `intarrays` pointer at `copy.cpp:82-84`. For a non-owning view, that pointer is the original source's backing list, so assignment to the view overwrites the source object.

Observed effect in release/default-style mode: assigning a same-size replacement through an `auto_destroy=false` view mutates the original source immediately, before any destructor or ownership cleanup path is involved:

```text
before_source=1111111122222222
assignment=returned
after_source=3333333344444444
view=3333333344444444
```

The same probe in debug mode confirms the intended guard exists, but is compiled out of release builds:

```text
before_source=1111111122222222
assignment_exception=Error in function "void unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into) const": num_to_paste_into appears to be a non-owning view (auto_destroy is false and intarrays is not null). Call forget_memory() on it first, otherwise copy_to would silently take ownership of shared storage.
after_source=1111111122222222
view=1111111122222222
```

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe.cpp`.

Build and run:

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=0 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe_release
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe_release

g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe_debug
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_assign_probe_debug
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #39. Finding #39 uses `auto_destroy_this=true` and the alias destructor frees another live integer's backing storage. This finding uses the intended non-owning mode (`auto_destroy_this=false`) and reaches the bug through public copy assignment; the original source is corrupted before the view is destroyed, and a fix that only rejects or disarms `auto_destroy_this=true` would not prevent this write-through assignment.

Status: confirmed by the release-mode derived-view reproducer with ASan/UBSan enabled. Promoted count is now 41.

### 42. Release-mode `copy_most_significant_to()` through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view corrupts shared storage metadata

Protected/documented route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102` and can be exposed by a derived class to create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another integer's storage. `copy_most_significant_to(unlimited_int&, size_t)` is also protected at `unlimited_int.hpp:128-130`; the comment says the destination "doesn't need to be prepared" and that the function creates an independent copy into that destination. A derived class can expose this helper directly.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source storage by copying `num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`. `copy_most_significant_to()` has the exact guard needed to reject a non-owning destination, but that guard is compiled only under `UNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE > 0` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:105-109`. In release/default builds the function continues, then treats the destination as writable storage: it sets destination metadata through the shared list at `copy.cpp:129-137`, writes copied limbs into that shared backing array at `copy.cpp:190-193`, and finalizes with `flush_unused()` at `copy.cpp:196`. Because an `auto_destroy=false` view has its own counters but points at the original object's `intarrays`, those writes mutate the original object's backing nodes without updating the original object's top-level counters.

Observed effect in release/default-style mode: the protected helper returns successfully, but the original aliased target is corrupted badly enough that reading it through public `to_string()` crashes under ASan/UBSan:

```text
before_target=11112222333344445555666677778888
copy_most_sig=returned
about_to_read_after_target
unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:58:45: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'struct int_array'
AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL
```

The crash stack shows the read of the original going through public `to_string()` (`unlimited/unlimited_int/to_string.cpp:23`), then copy construction (`unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:311`), then `copy_to()` walking into an end-sentinel/null `int_array` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:58`.

The same probe in debug mode confirms the intended guard exists and prevents the corruption:

```text
before_target=11112222333344445555666677778888
copy_most_sig_exception=Error in function "void unlimited_int::copy_most_significant_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into, const size_t num_of_ints_to_copy) const": num_to_paste_into appears to be a non-owning view (auto_destroy is false and intarrays is not null). Call forget_memory() on it first, otherwise the function would silently write through shared storage.
about_to_read_after_target
after_target=11112222333344445555666677778888
view=11112222333344445555666677778888
```

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe.cpp`.

Build and run:

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=0 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe_release
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe_release

g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe_debug
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_copy_most_sig_probe_debug
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #41. Finding #41 reaches `copy_to()` through public copy assignment and overwrites the original source value. This finding reaches `copy_most_significant_to()` through the documented protected helper and corrupts shared per-node storage metadata, causing a subsequent public read of the original object to crash. It is also not finding #39, because `auto_destroy_this=false` is used and no destructor/free path is involved.

Status: confirmed by the release-mode derived-helper reproducer with ASan/UBSan enabled and by the matching debug-mode guard output. Promoted count is now 42.

### 43. Public `flush()` / `destroy()` ignore `auto_destroy=false` and free another live integer through a non-owning view

Protected/documented route plus public cleanup route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy` in the new object. A derived class can expose this constructor and create a view with `auto_destroy_this=false`. The public manual cleanup methods `destroy()` and `flush()` are declared at `unlimited_int.hpp:632-640`.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by assigning `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`. The public cleanup methods do not respect the current ownership flag. `flush()` immediately sets `this->auto_destroy = true`, then flushes and deletes `this->intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.cpp:14-23`. `destroy()` does the same ownership override and deletes the backing list at `unlimited_int.cpp:25-34`. On an `auto_destroy=false` view, `this->intarrays` is the original object's backing list, so either public cleanup method frees/recycles another live integer's storage and leaves the original object with a dangling `intarrays` pointer.

### 44. Public arithmetic through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view can corrupt the original object's metadata and value

Protected/documented route plus public arithmetic route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says the constructor receives another integer "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose this constructor and create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another live integer. The inherited public arithmetic assignment `operator+=(const unlimited_int&)` is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:398-404` and calls the protected `add(..., this)` helper directly.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by copying `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`, but the view keeps independent top-level counters (`num_of_used_ints`, `num_of_intarrays_used`, and sign). In the multi-limb public `operator+=` path, `add()` creates read-only non-owning magnitude views of the operands at `unlimited/unlimited_int/addition.cpp:60-65`, then writes directly into `answer->intarrays` after `answer->increase_until_num_of_ints(...)` at `addition.cpp:105-107`. The limb writes happen at `addition.cpp:182-183` and the result metadata is committed only to `answer` at `addition.cpp:332-350`. When `answer` is the `auto_destroy=false` view, these writes mutate the original object's shared backing nodes, but the original object's top-level counters remain unchanged. A carry that increases the view's length therefore leaves the original object describing the old length over already-overwritten limbs.

Observed effect in a debug build: `view += 1` returns successfully, `view` reads as `0x10000000000000000`, but reading or copying the original source trips `find_inconsistencies()` because the original still reports the old two-limb length while its most-significant used limb is now zero:

```text
before_source=ffffffffffffffff
before_view=ffffffffffffffff
plus_equals=returned
after_source=
Error found by function "find_inconsistencies": The most significant digit in the whole "unlimited_int" type number is 0
after_source_exception=inconsistency found in the beginning of "void unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into) const"
after_view=10000000000000000
source_copy_exception=inconsistency found in the beginning of "void unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into) const"
```

Observed effect in a release/default-style build: the same public arithmetic call silently changes the original source's visible value from `0xffffffffffffffff` to `0`, while the view sees the mathematically expected carry result:

```text
before_source=ffffffffffffffff
before_view=ffffffffffffffff
plus_equals=returned
after_source=0
after_view=10000000000000000
source_copy=0
```

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe.cpp`.

Build and run:

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe_debug
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe_debug

g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=0 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=2 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe_release
/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_arithmetic_probe_release
```

Distinctness: this is not finding #41. Finding #41 reaches `copy_to()` through public copy assignment; release-mode assignment to the view overwrites the original source value through the copy helper. This finding reaches the normal public arithmetic mutator `operator+=`, which writes through the shared limb list and commits expanded-length metadata only to the view, leaving the original object's metadata inconsistent with the shared storage. It is also not finding #42's `copy_most_significant_to()` helper route and not #43's cleanup/free route. This entry intentionally groups the arithmetic-through-view metadata-divergence class as one finding rather than splitting every possible public mutator variant.

Status: confirmed by ASan/UBSan debug and release-style repros. Promoted count is now 44.

### 45. Public right shift through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view detaches nodes from the original object's shared list

Protected/documented route plus public shift route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says it receives another integer "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose that constructor and create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another live integer. The inherited public right-shift assignment operator is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:548` and calls `shift_right_by_bits()` directly.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by copying `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`, but the view and original keep independent top-level counters. For whole-limb shifts, public `operator>>=` reaches `shift_right_by_bits()`, which calls `shift_right()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_right.cpp:227`. `shift_right()` then calls `this->intarrays->flush_insignificant_to_piggy_bank(num_of_intarrays_went_through)` at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:201`, physically detaching least-significant nodes from the linked list that is shared with the original object, then updates only the view's counters at `bitwise_shift_right.cpp:203-204`. The original object still reports its old `num_of_used_ints` / `num_of_intarrays_used`, but the shared list no longer contains the nodes those counters require.

Observed effect in a debug build: `view >>= 32` returns successfully. Reading the original source afterward trips `find_inconsistencies()` because the original still reports four used limbs/nodes while the shared list now contains only three used limbs:

```text
before_source=11111111222222223333333344444444
before_view=11111111222222223333333344444444
shift_right=returned
after_source_exception=inconsistency found in the beginning of "void unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into) const"
after_view=111111112222222233333333
source_copy_exception=inconsistency found in the beginning of "void unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited_int& num_to_paste_into) const"
```

The debug diagnostic printed the underlying invariant failure:

```text
Error found by function "find_inconsistencies": the sum of the "num_of_used_ints" variables in the "int_array"s pointed to in "this->intarr.intarr" list, doesn't equal "this->num_of_used_ints" because the sum equals: 3 and the official variable "this->num_of_used_ints" equals: 4
```

Observed effect in a release/default-style build: the shift returns, then a public `to_string()` read of the original crashes under ASan/UBSan because `copy_to()` walks according to the original's stale counters and reaches the list sentinel/null value:

```text
before_source=11111111222222223333333344444444
before_view=11111111222222223333333344444444
shift_right=returned
after_source=unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:58:45: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'struct int_array'
AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL
#0 unlimited::unlimited_int::copy_to(unlimited::unlimited_int&) const unlimited/unlimited_int/copy.cpp:58
#1 unlimited::unlimited_int::unlimited_int(unlimited::unlimited_int const&) unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:311
#2 unlimited::unlimited_int::to_string(unsigned int) const unlimited/unlimited_int/to_string.cpp:23
#3 print_read /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe.cpp:21
#4 main /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe.cpp:44
```

Reproducer: `/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe.cpp`.

Build and run:

```bash

/tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe_debug

g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_DEBUG_MODE=0 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MIN_ALLOC=1 -DUNLIMITED_INT_LIBRARY_MAX_ALLOC=1 -I. /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe.cpp $(rg --files unlimited | rg '\.cpp$') -o /tmp/unlimited_int_nonowning_shift_probe_release

Distinctness: this is not finding #44. Finding #44 uses public arithmetic to overwrite shared limb values and commits expanded-length metadata only to the view. This finding uses public right shift to splice nodes out of the shared linked list itself through `flush_insignificant_to_piggy_bank()`, so the original object's stale counters can drive a sentinel/null-node walk and release-mode crash on the next public read. It is also not #43's public cleanup/free route: the call here is a normal shift operation, not `flush()` or `destroy()`.

### 46. Public left shift through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view prepends nodes into the original object's shared list and silently changes the original value

Protected/documented route plus public shift route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says it receives another integer "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose that constructor and create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another live integer. The inherited public left-shift assignment operator is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:547` and calls `shift_left_by_bits()` directly.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by copying `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`, but the view and original keep independent top-level counters. For whole-limb shifts, public `operator<<=` reaches `shift_left_by_bits()`, which calls `shift_left()` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/bitwise_shift_left.cpp:91-92`. `shift_left()` builds a new list of zero-filled least-significant nodes at `bitwise_shift_left.cpp:33-57`, then prepends that list into `this->intarrays` at `bitwise_shift_left.cpp:62-65` and updates only `this->num_of_used_ints` at `bitwise_shift_left.cpp:67`. When `this` is an `auto_destroy=false` view, the prepend happens to the original object's shared linked list, but the original object's counters are not updated. ```text

before_view=1111111122222222
shift_left=returned
after_source=2222222200000000
after_view=111111112222222200000000
source_copy=2222222200000000
```

### 48. Public move assignment from an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view of the destination installs a dangling backing-list pointer

Protected/documented route plus public move-assignment route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says it receives another integer "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose that constructor and create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another live integer. The inherited public move assignment operator is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:326-327`.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by copying `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`. Public move assignment first flushes the destination when it is owning at `unlimited/unlimited_int/move_unlimited_int.cpp:4-7`; `flush()` deletes `this->intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.cpp:14-24`. If the move source is an `auto_destroy=false` view of that same destination, the view's `intarrays` pointer aliases the just-deleted list. The move assignment then copies `source.intarrays` into the destination at `move_unlimited_int.cpp:8-12` and only afterward calls `source.forget_memory()` at `move_unlimited_int.cpp:13`. The destination now stores a dangling pointer and `auto_destroy=false`.

Observed effect in a debug build: `source = std::move(view)` returns, but the first public read of `source` after the assignment reaches freed storage during the debug consistency check:

### 49. Public `power2_destroy_this()` through an `auto_destroy=false` non-owning view frees the original object's backing list

Protected/documented route plus public destructive-squaring route: `unlimited_int::unlimited_int(const unlimited_int&, bool)` is declared in the protected section at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:100-102`; the header says it receives another integer "without copying" and that the second parameter decides whether to enable `auto_destroy`. A derived class can expose that constructor and create an `auto_destroy=false` view of another live integer. The public destructive squaring API is declared at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.hpp:366-369` as `power2_destroy_this()`.

Root: the non-owning constructor aliases the source backing list by copying `this->intarrays = num_to_assign.intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/constructors.cpp:6-12`. For inputs above the Karatsuba squaring threshold, public `power2_destroy_this()` calls `this->split_at_and_use_original(m2, &high, &low)` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/multiplication_Karatsuba.cpp:244-247`. That split helper operates on `this->intarrays` directly: it detaches nodes from the shared list into `low` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/split_at.cpp:261-263`, later transfers remaining high-side nodes at `split_at.cpp:342-343`, and finally calls `this->flush()` at `split_at.cpp:348`. `flush()` deletes `this->intarrays` at `unlimited/unlimited_int/unlimited_int.cpp:14-24`. When `this` is an `auto_destroy=false` view, all of that is happening to the original object's shared backing list, while the original object's `intarrays` pointer and counters remain unchanged.
